destination.name: New England National Park
destination.tagline: Escarpment park in the Gondwana Rainforests World Heritage Area, with lookouts, waterfalls and granite country around it.
destination.description: New England National Park covers 67,303 hectares on the Northern Tablelands, 85 km east of Armidale and 65 km west of Coffs Harbour. It was created in 1935 and is part of the Gondwana Rainforests of Australia, inscribed in 1986. Walks range from a 200 m stroll to multi-day hikes, passing snow gum forest where crimson rosellas feed. Nearby parks and falls add Cathedral Rock's granite tors and Ebor Falls on the Guy Fawkes River.

goodToKnow.title: Cathedral Rock loop
goodToKnow.detail: The 6 km loop to the boulder summit is in a park that may close at times for poor weather or fire danger.

goodToKnow.title: Cunnawarra is remote
goodToKnow.detail: Cunnawarra National Park is remote, with 4WD tracks, so check conditions before heading out.

goodToKnow.title: Download maps first
goodToKnow.detail: NSW National Parks says its free app lets you download maps without mobile reception.
